doc.title: Jerry Hey interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, November 2, 2023

title: Childhood listening: records bought by his father
summary: Hey listened to his father's records, such as Clifford Brown, rather than AM radio; his brother played trombone.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up with radio, records and family listening

blocks.x: When you think about growing up and listening to the radio, let’s say by the time you were ten, twelve, do you recall the variety of music that you could absorb through AM radio back then?

You know I didn’t really listen to AM radio until probably I got to high school or maybe seventh or eighth grade you know and kind of The Beatles came in and you know, so that’s kind of the first AM radio that I listened to. For the most part I was listening to records that my dad had bought.

Which were — he heard Clifford Brown live in 1954 I believe, in Chicago. I’m from Illinois. So he went into Chicago and heard Clifford Brown live and then bought his first, it was a ten inch record then, it came out a 33 RPM but it was ten inches, and it had the original version of “Cherokee” on it and “Easy Living” and some great stuff. So I had that, and then as Clifford Brown records came out my dad would buy those and some other Dixieland and some — my older brother had some records of Frank Rossolino. My brother was a trombone player. So there was a lot of listening to records more than listening to AM radio.
Well that’s fortunate for your musical tastes I think.
That’s a pretty hip place to start.
